jen: Thanks for the questions in today's all-hands. Pulling a short Q&A here about region capacity, autoscale behavior, and what customers should expect.

alex: For customer comms: what's the short fallback order (single-line)?

maria: Fallback order (short): in-region warm lane -> same-region alternate SKU/quantized variant -> nearest healthy region -> reserved/dedicated pool (if committed) -> model-family downgrade only if customer opts in.

akex: Typo 😅 meant alex. Next: does cross-region routing affect regional latency SLAs?

rebecca: Cross-region is "best-effort continuity" and not counted toward strict regional latency SLAs. Enterprise customers can buy multi-region reserved capacity or add an SLA appendix for cross-region guarantees.

tia: How long to prewarm large models and do we bill for warm lanes?

maria: Prewarm typical: ~30s–3m depending on model/SKU. Billing: reserved credits cover warm lanes for committed customers; on-demand prewarm billed as small warm allocation + compute while active. We'll add a FAQ line.

kyle: Ops note / sample policy we use internally:
```
routing_policy: { prefer_in_region: true, sku_sequence: [a100-80g,a100-40g,t4-16g], cross_region_threshold: 0.2, latency_budget_ms: 150 }
```

alex: If a request switches models mid-stream, how will billing and telemetry appear?

rebecca: Tokens are attributed to the producing model. Billing console will show per-request model/token split and unit price lines so customers see exactly what ran.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: region-fallback policy canary adjusted to 45% by @kyle at 14:21.

jen: Action items: kyle drafts public FAQ blurb about billing & fallbacks; maria writes internal handoff semantics (KV transfer / continuation prompt); rebecca verifies billing UI shows per-model splits; I'll sync comms for a brief customer note. Drop any tough customer examples here and we'll fold them in.
